beats: Hook (line_qc_catch_two_strips, then the cover): checks and errors are both just strings like XZZXI. Whether an error is caught comes down to one count: in how many positions do the two strings clash? Odd means caught. Code letters I/X/Y/Z on the blank cards; one worked count on screen at a time (the syllabus note: the heaviest QEC part). Cast as in QC08-01 to QC08-04 (Q25-11 continues Q25-10's story, so the lecture keeps that cast), described in full in every prompt: the keeper = the code (encodes, checks, fixes) and the imp = the noise. The props stay too: wall plates with closed flaps = data qubits, bulbs = checks (QC08-02's convention: a lit bulb = the check reads -1), round glasses = the 0/1 (Z) lens, square glasses = the +/- (X) lens (QC08-03). Say once that real errors are random, not a prankster: the imp only stands for chance. Invented characters only: no lecturer figure, never her likeness, no portrait of Shor, Steane, Hamming or anyone real. All of QC08-05 to QC08-08 reference line_qc_vote_switch_fix (QC08-01): make it first.

Why Pauli operators (Q25-11 30:40-33:50): X, Y, Z are Hermitian and unitary at once, so the same check works as a gate and as a measurement (callback QC06-01); their eigenvalues are only +1 and -1, so the measuring circuit is the simple one of QC06-02; fixing X and Z fixes everything (QC08-04). Tape Q24-11 s7 (the Q25-11 frames carry an old institution's footer: prefer the Q24-11 frames or crop it).

The Pauli group (33:53-38:58; Q24-11 08:04-14:12): 4^n strings on n qubits; any two either commute or anticommute; weight = the positions that are not I. The clash count: each position where both are non-I and different flips the sign once, so only the parity of the count matters (reuse line_qc_build_stair_switches from QC05-06: every flip toggles the lamp, an even number leaves it as it was). Worked on the five-qubit checks (22:18-25:59): XZZXI against IXZZX clash twice, so they commute.

Checks are symmetries of the good state: applying one changes nothing, like turning a snowflake by one arm (line_qc_catch_snowflake_turn); so all checks must commute with each other (an abelian group), and n qubits with n - k independent checks keep k logical qubits (38:58-42:16; Q24-11 15:58-22:03). The company named at 41:49-42:16 stays off screen and out of the narration.

Detection (42:16-47:16; Q24-11 22:06-27:27): an error that anticommutes with a check flips that check from +1 to -1, its bulb lights; the pattern of lit bulbs is the syndrome. Repetition code: X1 lights Z1Z2 only, X2 lights both (reuse line_qc_synd_read_bulbs from QC08-02); the five-qubit code has four bulbs (line_qc_catch_four_bulbs; code letters which error lit which pair).

Why X errors need Z checks (clip 46:01-46:52, "X always commutes with X"): an X never clashes with an X, so an all-X check cannot see an X error; in QC08-03's picture language a flip is seen only through the lens it was made in (reuse line_qc_shor_unseen_trick and line_qc_shor_glasses_catch). Caption: Y clashes with both X and Z, so it is seen through either lens.

Silent logical errors (47:16-52:12; Q24-11 27:31-33:23): errors that commute with every check but are not checks, N(S) minus S; X1X2X3 turns 000 into 111, a valid codeword, and every bulb stays dark (clip 50:10-50:37, "a logical error we cannot detect") (line_qc_catch_all_three_flipped). Caption: it needs three flips at once, rare (about p^3). The distance d is the weight of the smallest such error.

Detect vs correct (52:12-54:30): d = 2t + 1; the repetition code detects two flips and corrects one; Shor's code is [[9,1,3]] (line_qc_catch_two_villages: one hop from home and you are walked back; two hops and the nearer village is the wrong one; three and nobody notices; code adds 000, 111 and the footprints). The correction condition (Q24-11 33:29-56:14, advanced; skip the quiz 46:37-52:38): one line only.

Code design is an optimisation over n, k, d: for the same n, a bigger k and a bigger d (61:18-62:46; clip Q24-11 06:54-07:40, "the design space is huge: where computer science comes in") (line_qc_catch_brick_houses: the same heap of bricks, many rooms with thin walls or one room with thick walls).
Cover (line_qc_cover_08_05; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the keeper counts clashes between two strips of cards; the imp peeks over the table edge.
